description: Digital modulation and demodulation, OFDM, channel models and impairments, pulse shaping, error-control coding, error-rate measurement and communications visualization.

tools.name: qammod
tools.description: Modulate integer symbols or bits onto a rectangular QAM constellation of a given order. Options control Gray or binary symbol mapping, unit average power normalization and whether the input is bits. It is the standard modulator for 16-QAM, 64-QAM and 256-QAM links.
tools.usage:
y = qammod(x, M)
y = qammod(x, M, symorder)
y = qammod(x, M, Name, Value)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Integer symbols in 0..M-1, or a bit vector when 'InputType' is 'bit'.

parameters.name: M
parameters.description: Modulation order; must be a power of two.

parameters.name: symorder
parameters.description: 'gray' (default) or 'bin' symbol mapping.

parameters.name: 'UnitAveragePower'
parameters.description: Logical; normalize the constellation to unit average power.

parameters.name: 'InputType'
parameters.description: 'integer' (default) or 'bit'.

parameters.name: 'PlotConstellation'
parameters.description: Logical; display the constellation diagram.

tools.notes: Use the same 'UnitAveragePower' and symbol-order settings in qammod and qamdemod or the results will be wrong.

tools.name: qamdemod
tools.description: Demodulate a QAM signal back to integer symbols or bits, with hard decisions or approximate/exact log-likelihood ratios for soft-decision decoding. The LLR output modes feed directly into LDPC, turbo and Viterbi soft decoders. Settings must mirror those used by qammod.
tools.usage:
z = qamdemod(y, M)
z = qamdemod(y, M, symorder)
z = qamdemod(y, M, Name, Value)

parameters.name: M
parameters.description: Modulation order.

parameters.name: symorder
parameters.description: 'gray' (default) or 'bin'.

parameters.name: 'OutputType'
parameters.description: 'integer' (default), 'bit', 'llr' or 'approxllr'.

parameters.name: 'NoiseVariance'
parameters.description: Noise variance, required for the LLR output types.

parameters.name: 'UnitAveragePower'
parameters.description: Must match the modulator setting.

tools.name: pskmod
tools.description: Modulate symbols onto an M-ary phase-shift-keying constellation with a configurable initial phase offset. BPSK, QPSK and 8-PSK are the common cases, and a pi/4 offset gives the familiar rotated QPSK constellation. PSK has a constant envelope, which suits nonlinear power amplifiers.
tools.usage:
y = pskmod(x, M)
y = pskmod(x, M, phaseoffset)
y = pskmod(x, M, phaseoffset, symorder)
y = pskmod(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: M
parameters.description: Modulation order (2 for BPSK, 4 for QPSK, 8 for 8-PSK).

parameters.name: phaseoffset
parameters.description: Constellation rotation in radians, e.g. pi/4.

parameters.name: symorder
parameters.description: 'gray' (default) or 'bin'.

parameters.name: 'InputType'
parameters.description: 'integer' (default) or 'bit'.

tools.name: pskdemod
tools.description: Demodulate an M-PSK signal to integer symbols, bits or log-likelihood ratios. The phase offset and symbol order must match those used at the transmitter. Soft LLR output enables coded systems to gain several dB over hard decisions.
tools.usage:
z = pskdemod(y, M)
z = pskdemod(y, M, phaseoffset)
z = pskdemod(y, M, phaseoffset, symorder)
z = pskdemod(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: M
parameters.description: Modulation order.

parameters.name: phaseoffset
parameters.description: Must match the modulator.

parameters.name: 'OutputType'
parameters.description: 'integer', 'bit', 'llr' or 'approxllr'.

parameters.name: 'NoiseVariance'
parameters.description: Required for LLR output.

tools.name: ofdmmod
tools.description: Perform OFDM modulation: map frequency-domain symbols onto subcarriers, take an IFFT and prepend a cyclic prefix. Null and pilot subcarrier positions can be specified so the output matches a real standard's frame structure. It is the core transmit operation for LTE, 5G NR, Wi-Fi and DVB waveforms.
tools.usage:
y = ofdmmod(x, nfft, cplen)
y = ofdmmod(x, nfft, cplen, nullidx)
y = ofdmmod(x, nfft, cplen, nullidx, pilotidx, pilots)
y = ofdmmod(___, 'OversamplingFactor', osf)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Frequency-domain symbols, size (nfft - numNull) by numSymbols by numTx.

parameters.name: nfft
parameters.description: FFT length, equal to the number of subcarriers.

parameters.name: cplen
parameters.description: Cyclic prefix length in samples, scalar or per-symbol vector.

parameters.name: nullidx
parameters.description: Indices of null (guard and DC) subcarriers.

parameters.name: pilotidx, pilots
parameters.description: Pilot subcarrier indices and pilot symbol values.

tools.name: ofdmdemod
tools.description: Perform OFDM demodulation: remove the cyclic prefix, take an FFT and extract the data subcarriers, optionally returning the pilot subcarriers separately. Parameters must match those used by ofdmmod. The extracted pilots are what a channel estimator uses.
tools.usage:
y = ofdmdemod(x, nfft, cplen)
y = ofdmdemod(x, nfft, cplen, symoffset)
y = ofdmdemod(x, nfft, cplen, symoffset, nullidx)
[y, pilots] = ofdmdemod(x, nfft, cplen, symoffset, nullidx, pilotidx)

parameters.name: nfft, cplen
parameters.description: Must match the modulator settings.

parameters.name: symoffset
parameters.description: Sample offset into the cyclic prefix at which the FFT window starts.

parameters.name: nullidx
parameters.description: Null subcarrier indices to discard.

parameters.name: pilotidx
parameters.description: Pilot subcarrier indices to return separately.

tools.name: awgn
tools.description: Add white Gaussian noise to a signal at a specified signal-to-noise ratio. The 'measured' option computes the actual signal power first, which is what you normally want; otherwise a signal power must be supplied. It is the standard way to build a simple AWGN channel for BER simulations.
tools.usage:
out = awgn(in, snr)
out = awgn(in, snr, signalpower)
out = awgn(in, snr, 'measured')
out = awgn(___, seed, powertype)

parameters.name: snr
parameters.description: Signal-to-noise ratio in dB.

parameters.name: signalpower
parameters.description: Input signal power in dBW, or 'measured' to compute it.

parameters.name: powertype
parameters.description: 'db' (default) or 'linear'.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Random number generator seed or state, for reproducibility.

tools.notes: Remember the Eb/No to SNR conversion: SNR = EbNo + 10*log10(bitsPerSymbol) - 10*log10(samplesPerSymbol).

tools.name: comm.AWGNChannel
tools.description: A System object that adds white Gaussian noise, configurable by SNR, Eb/No, Es/No or an explicit noise variance. Unlike the awgn function it keeps its random stream state between calls, which is essential for correct streaming simulations. It also supports variable noise levels driven by an input port.
tools.usage:
chan = comm.AWGNChannel
chan = comm.AWGNChannel(Name, Value)
y = chan(x)
release(chan); reset(chan)

parameters.name: 'NoiseMethod'
parameters.description: 'Signal to noise ratio (Eb/No)', '(Es/No)', '(SNR)' or 'Variance'.

parameters.name: 'EbNo' / 'EsNo' / 'SNR'
parameters.description: Noise level in dB for the chosen method.

parameters.name: 'BitsPerSymbol'
parameters.description: Bits per symbol, needed for the Eb/No method.

parameters.name: 'SamplesPerSymbol'
parameters.description: Oversampling factor of the input signal.

parameters.name: 'SignalPower'
parameters.description: Input signal power in watts.

parameters.name: 'RandomStream' / 'Seed'
parameters.description: Noise generator configuration for reproducible runs.

tools.name: comm.RayleighChannel
tools.description: Model a multipath Rayleigh fading channel with configurable path delays, average path gains and maximum Doppler shift. Rayleigh fading represents a non-line-of-sight environment where no single path dominates. Standard delay profiles and the path-gain output make it easy to study equalization and diversity.
tools.usage:
chan = comm.RayleighChannel(Name, Value)
y = chan(x)
[y, pathGains] = chan(x)
release(chan); reset(chan); info(chan)

parameters.name: 'SampleRate'
parameters.description: Input signal sample rate in Hz.

parameters.name: 'PathDelays'
parameters.description: Vector of path delays in seconds.

parameters.name: 'AveragePathGains'
parameters.description: Average gain of each path in dB.

parameters.name: 'MaximumDopplerShift'
parameters.description: Maximum Doppler in Hz; 0 gives a static channel.

parameters.name: 'DopplerSpectrum'
parameters.description: doppler('Jakes'), doppler('Flat'), doppler('Gaussian'), etc.

parameters.name: 'PathGainsOutputPort'
parameters.description: Logical; also return the complex path gains.

parameters.name: 'NormalizePathGains'
parameters.description: Logical; keep the total average power at 0 dB.

tools.name: comm.RicianChannel
tools.description: Model a multipath fading channel with a dominant line-of-sight component, parameterized by the K-factor giving the ratio of specular to diffuse power. A large K-factor approaches an AWGN channel while K near zero approaches Rayleigh. Use it for satellite, microcell and indoor line-of-sight links.
tools.usage:
chan = comm.RicianChannel(Name, Value)
y = chan(x)
[y, pathGains] = chan(x)

parameters.name: 'KFactor'
parameters.description: Rician K-factor in linear units; scalar or one value per path.

parameters.name: 'DirectPathDopplerShift'
parameters.description: Doppler shift of the line-of-sight component in Hz.

parameters.name: 'DirectPathInitialPhase'
parameters.description: Initial phase of the direct path in radians.

parameters.name: 'PathDelays' / 'AveragePathGains'
parameters.description: Multipath profile.

parameters.name: 'MaximumDopplerShift'
parameters.description: Maximum Doppler in Hz.

parameters.name: 'SampleRate'
parameters.description: Signal sample rate.

tools.name: rcosdesign
tools.description: Design a raised-cosine or square-root raised-cosine FIR pulse-shaping filter. Root-raised-cosine filters are used in matched pairs at transmitter and receiver so the combined response satisfies the Nyquist zero-ISI criterion. The rolloff factor trades excess bandwidth against time-domain tail decay.
tools.usage:
b = rcosdesign(beta, span, sps)
b = rcosdesign(beta, span, sps, shape)

parameters.name: beta
parameters.description: Rolloff factor between 0 and 1; typical values are 0.22 to 0.35.

parameters.name: span
parameters.description: Filter length in symbols (an even number, usually 6 to 10).

parameters.name: sps
parameters.description: Samples per symbol (oversampling factor).

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: 'sqrt' (default, root raised cosine) or 'normal'.

tools.notes: The total group delay of a matched RRC pair is span symbols; discard span/2 symbols at each end.

tools.name: comm.RaisedCosineTransmitFilter
tools.description: A System object that upsamples and pulse-shapes a symbol stream with a raised-cosine or root-raised-cosine filter in one efficient polyphase step. It maintains filter state between calls, which makes it correct for frame-by-frame streaming simulations. Its coefficients can be inspected and its response visualized with fvtool.
tools.usage:
txfilter = comm.RaisedCosineTransmitFilter(Name, Value)
y = txfilter(x)
coeffs(txfilter)
fvtool(txfilter)

parameters.name: 'Shape'
parameters.description: 'Square root' (default) or 'Normal'.

parameters.name: 'RolloffFactor'
parameters.description: Excess bandwidth factor, default 0.2.

parameters.name: 'FilterSpanInSymbols'
parameters.description: Filter length in symbol periods, default 10.

parameters.name: 'OutputSamplesPerSymbol'
parameters.description: Upsampling factor, default 8.

parameters.name: 'Gain'
parameters.description: Overall filter gain, often set to normalize output power.

tools.name: comm.RaisedCosineReceiveFilter
tools.description: A System object that applies the matched raised-cosine receive filter and optionally decimates back to the symbol rate. Paired with comm.RaisedCosineTransmitFilter it forms an ISI-free Nyquist channel. Setting the decimation factor lower than the oversampling ratio leaves samples for a timing synchronizer.
tools.usage:
rxfilter = comm.RaisedCosineReceiveFilter(Name, Value)
y = rxfilter(x)
coeffs(rxfilter)

parameters.name: 'RolloffFactor'
parameters.description: Must match the transmit filter.

parameters.name: 'FilterSpanInSymbols'
parameters.description: Filter length in symbols.

parameters.name: 'InputSamplesPerSymbol'
parameters.description: Oversampling factor of the incoming signal.

parameters.name: 'DecimationFactor'
parameters.description: Output decimation; set to InputSamplesPerSymbol for one sample per symbol.

parameters.name: 'DecimationOffset'
parameters.description: Sample offset within each symbol period.

tools.name: biterr
tools.description: Count bit errors between transmitted and received data and compute the bit error rate. Inputs can be bit vectors or integer symbols, in which case each integer is compared bit by bit. Column-wise and row-wise comparison modes support multi-channel simulations.
tools.usage:
[number, ratio] = biterr(x, y)
[number, ratio, individual] = biterr(x, y, k)
[___] = biterr(x, y, k, flag)

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: Transmitted and received data, as bits or nonnegative integers.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Number of bits per element when comparing integers.

parameters.name: flag
parameters.description: 'overall' (default), 'column-wise' or 'row-wise'.

tools.name: symerr
tools.description: Count symbol errors and compute the symbol error rate between two data sets. A symbol counts as an error if it differs at all, regardless of how many of its bits are wrong. Use it alongside biterr to see the benefit of Gray mapping.
tools.usage:
[number, ratio] = symerr(x, y)
[number, ratio, individual] = symerr(x, y, flag)

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: Transmitted and received symbol arrays.

parameters.name: flag
parameters.description: 'overall' (default), 'column-wise' or 'row-wise'.

tools.name: berawgn
tools.description: Compute the theoretical bit error rate of a modulation scheme over an AWGN channel as a function of Eb/No. Comparing a simulated BER curve against this theoretical reference is the standard way to validate a link simulation. It covers PSK, QAM, FSK, PAM, DPSK and MSK.
tools.usage:
ber = berawgn(EbNo, modType, M)
ber = berawgn(EbNo, 'psk', M, dataenc)
ber = berawgn(EbNo, 'fsk', M, coherence)
[ber, ser] = berawgn(___)

parameters.name: EbNo
parameters.description: Bit-energy-to-noise-density ratio in dB.

parameters.name: modType
parameters.description: 'psk', 'dpsk', 'oqpsk', 'pam', 'qam', 'fsk', 'msk'.

parameters.name: M
parameters.description: Modulation order.

parameters.name: dataenc
parameters.description: 'nondiff' (default) or 'diff' for differentially encoded PSK.

tools.notes: berfading, bercoding and bersync give theoretical curves for fading channels, coded systems and imperfect synchronization.

tools.name: bertool
tools.description: Open the Bit Error Rate Analysis app, which plots theoretical, semi-analytic and simulated BER curves on one set of axes. It can run your own simulation function over a range of Eb/No values and fit the results. Useful for producing publication-quality link performance comparisons.
tools.usage:
bertool
bertool('close')

parameters.name: 'close'
parameters.description: Close the app programmatically.

tools.example:
bertool
% Theoretical tab: choose QAM, order 16, AWGN, Eb/No 0:14
% Monte Carlo tab: point at your own simulation function
% Then export the BER data to the workspace
tools.notes: Requires a display. For scripted studies use berawgn, berfading and your own loop instead.

tools.name: poly2trellis
tools.description: Convert convolutional code polynomials, given in octal, into the trellis structure used by convenc, vitdec and the turbo and APP decoders. Constraint length and generator polynomials fully define a feedforward code; a feedback polynomial makes it recursive systematic. Its output is a plain structure you can inspect.
tools.usage:
trellis = poly2trellis(ConstraintLength, CodeGenerator)
trellis = poly2trellis(ConstraintLength, CodeGenerator, FeedbackConnection)

parameters.name: ConstraintLength
parameters.description: Constraint length per input stream, e.g. 7.

parameters.name: CodeGenerator
parameters.description: Matrix of generator polynomials in octal, e.g. [171 133].

parameters.name: FeedbackConnection
parameters.description: Octal feedback polynomial for recursive systematic codes.

tools.name: convenc
tools.description: Encode binary data with a convolutional code described by a trellis structure. Puncturing via a puncture pattern raises the code rate, and the encoder state can be carried between calls for streaming. Convolutional codes paired with Viterbi decoding are ubiquitous in wireless standards.
tools.usage:
codedout = convenc(msg, trellis)
codedout = convenc(msg, trellis, puncpat)
[codedout, fstate] = convenc(msg, trellis, istate)
[codedout, fstate] = convenc(msg, trellis, puncpat, istate)

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Binary input message vector.

parameters.name: trellis
parameters.description: Trellis structure from poly2trellis.

parameters.name: puncpat
parameters.description: Binary puncture pattern; 0 entries delete the corresponding coded bits.

parameters.name: istate / fstate
parameters.description: Initial and final encoder state, for block-by-block encoding.

tools.name: vitdec
tools.description: Decode convolutionally encoded data with the Viterbi maximum-likelihood algorithm, using hard, unquantized or soft-decision inputs. Soft-decision decoding typically buys around 2 dB over hard decisions. The traceback depth trades decoding delay and memory against performance; five times the constraint length is a common rule of thumb.
tools.usage:
decoded = vitdec(code, trellis, tblen, opmode, dectype)
decoded = vitdec(code, trellis, tblen, opmode, 'soft', nsdec)
decoded = vitdec(___, puncpat)

parameters.name: tblen
parameters.description: Traceback depth in symbols.

parameters.name: opmode
parameters.description: 'trunc', 'term' (encoder terminated to the all-zero state) or 'cont'.

parameters.name: dectype
parameters.description: 'hard', 'unquant' or 'soft'.

parameters.name: nsdec
parameters.description: Number of soft-decision bits, required for 'soft'.

parameters.name: puncpat
parameters.description: Puncture pattern matching the encoder.

tools.notes: For 'unquant' soft decoding, positive LLR must correspond to a 0 bit; negate if your demodulator uses the opposite convention.

tools.name: comm.LDPCEncoder
tools.description: Encode binary messages with a low-density parity-check code defined by a sparse parity-check matrix. LDPC codes achieve performance within a fraction of a dB of the Shannon limit at long block lengths and are used in DVB-S2, Wi-Fi and 5G. Pair it with comm.LDPCDecoder, which performs iterative belief propagation on soft LLR inputs.
tools.usage:
enc = comm.LDPCEncoder
enc = comm.LDPCEncoder(parityCheckMatrix)
codeword = enc(message)
dec = comm.LDPCDecoder(parityCheckMatrix)
message = dec(llr)

parameters.name: 'ParityCheckMatrix'
parameters.description: Sparse logical parity-check matrix; defaults to the DVB-S2 rate-3/4 matrix.

parameters.name: 'MaximumIterationCount'
parameters.description: Decoder iteration limit (default 50).

parameters.name: 'DecisionMethod'
parameters.description: 'Hard decision' (default) or 'Soft decision'.

parameters.name: 'IterationTerminationCondition'
parameters.description: 'Maximum iteration count' or 'Parity check satisfied'.

tools.notes: Newer releases provide the function-based ldpcEncoderConfig/ldpcEncode and ldpcDecoderConfig/ldpcDecode API, which is faster and preferred for new code.

tools.name: comm.TurboEncoder
tools.description: Encode data with a parallel-concatenated turbo code built from two recursive systematic convolutional encoders separated by an interleaver. Turbo codes approach capacity through iterative decoding and are used in 3G/4G standards. comm.TurboDecoder performs the iterative MAP decoding on soft LLR inputs.
tools.usage:
tEnc = comm.TurboEncoder(trellis, interleaverIndices)
codeword = tEnc(data)
tDec = comm.TurboDecoder(trellis, interleaverIndices, numIter)
data = tDec(llr)

parameters.name: 'TrellisStructure'
parameters.description: Recursive systematic trellis, e.g. poly2trellis(4, [13 15], 13).

parameters.name: 'InterleaverIndices'
parameters.description: Permutation vector applied before the second constituent encoder.

parameters.name: 'NumIterations'
parameters.description: Decoder iterations (default 6); more gives better performance at higher cost.

parameters.name: 'Algorithm'
parameters.description: 'True APP', 'Max*' or 'Max' decoding approximation.

tools.name: comm.CRCGenerator
tools.description: Append a cyclic redundancy check to a binary message for error detection. The polynomial, initial state, final XOR value and bit reflection settings let you match any standard CRC such as CRC-8, CRC-16-CCITT or CRC-32. comm.CRCDetector at the receiver strips the checksum and reports whether an error was detected.
tools.usage:
crcGen = comm.CRCGenerator(polynomial)
crcGen = comm.CRCGenerator(Name, Value)
codeword = crcGen(msg)
crcDet = comm.CRCDetector(polynomial)
[msg, err] = crcDet(codeword)

parameters.name: 'Polynomial'
parameters.description: Generator polynomial as a binary vector, octal string or 'z^16 + z^12 + z^5 + 1' style expression.

parameters.name: 'InitialConditions'
parameters.description: Initial shift-register state, 0 or 1 or a vector.

parameters.name: 'DirectMethod'
parameters.description: Logical; use the direct CRC algorithm.

parameters.name: 'ReflectInputBytes' / 'ReflectChecksums'
parameters.description: Bit-reflection options needed to match many standards.

parameters.name: 'FinalXOR'
parameters.description: Value XORed with the computed checksum.

parameters.name: 'ChecksumsPerFrame'
parameters.description: Number of checksums appended per frame.

tools.name: rsenc
tools.description: Encode a Galois field message array with a Reed-Solomon block code, appending parity symbols. Reed-Solomon codes correct bursts of symbol errors and underpin CDs, DVDs, QR codes and deep-space links. An (n, k) code corrects up to (n-k)/2 symbol errors.
tools.usage:
code = rsenc(msg, n, k)
code = rsenc(msg, n, k, genpoly)
code = rsenc(___, parityPos)

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Galois field array with k columns, created with gf().

parameters.name: n, k
parameters.description: Codeword and message lengths in symbols; n = 2^m - 1 for a full-length code.

parameters.name: genpoly
parameters.description: Generator polynomial from rsgenpoly, for shortened or custom codes.

parameters.name: parityPos
parameters.description: 'end' (default) or 'beginning'.

tools.name: rsdec
tools.description: Decode a Reed-Solomon codeword, correcting symbol errors and reporting how many were corrected per codeword. A value of -1 in the error count means the codeword had too many errors to correct. Erasure positions can be supplied, which doubles the correction capability for known-bad symbols.
tools.usage:
decoded = rsdec(code, n, k)
[decoded, cnumerr] = rsdec(code, n, k)
[decoded, cnumerr, ccode] = rsdec(code, n, k, genpoly)
[___] = rsdec(___, erasures)

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Received Galois field codeword array.

parameters.name: n, k
parameters.description: Code parameters, matching the encoder.

parameters.name: genpoly
parameters.description: Generator polynomial for shortened codes.

parameters.name: erasures
parameters.description: Binary array marking known erased symbol positions.

tools.name: comm.ErrorRate
tools.description: A System object that accumulates error statistics across many calls, returning the running error rate, error count and total symbol count. Because it keeps state, it is the correct way to measure BER over a multi-frame simulation. Receive delay and computation delay options align the transmitted and received streams.
tools.usage:
errorRate = comm.ErrorRate
errorRate = comm.ErrorRate(Name, Value)
stats = errorRate(txData, rxData)
reset(errorRate)

parameters.name: 'ReceiveDelay'
parameters.description: Number of samples of delay in the received signal relative to the transmitted one.

parameters.name: 'ComputationDelay'
parameters.description: Samples to ignore at the start while the system settles.

parameters.name: 'ResetInputPort'
parameters.description: Logical; add an input that resets the counters.

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: Three-element vector [errorRate, numErrors, numSymbols].

tools.name: comm.PNSequence
tools.description: Generate a pseudo-noise (maximal-length) binary sequence from a linear feedback shift register defined by a generator polynomial. PN sequences are used for spreading in CDMA, for scrambling, for synchronization preambles and as repeatable test data. The mask or shift setting selects the phase of the sequence.
tools.usage:
pn = comm.PNSequence(Name, Value)
seq = pn()
reset(pn); release(pn)

parameters.name: 'Polynomial'
parameters.description: LFSR generator polynomial, e.g. [1 0 0 0 0 1 1] or 'x^6 + x + 1'.

parameters.name: 'InitialConditions'
parameters.description: Initial shift-register state; must not be all zeros.

parameters.name: 'SamplesPerFrame'
parameters.description: Number of output bits per call.

parameters.name: 'Mask' / 'InitialConditionsSource'
parameters.description: Phase selection and state source.

parameters.name: 'VariableSizeOutput'
parameters.description: Logical; allow the output length to vary per call.

tools.name: scatterplot
tools.description: Plot the in-phase and quadrature components of a complex signal as a constellation scatter plot. Decimation and offset arguments let you plot only the symbol-rate samples of an oversampled signal. It is the quickest visual check of noise, phase error and gain imbalance.
tools.usage:
scatterplot(x)
scatterplot(x, n)
scatterplot(x, n, offset)
h = scatterplot(x, n, offset, plotstring)
scatterplot(x, n, offset, plotstring, h)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Complex signal, or a two-column real matrix of I and Q.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Decimation factor, typically the samples per symbol.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of initial samples to skip.

parameters.name: plotstring
parameters.description: Line style and colour specification such as 'r.'.

tools.name: eyediagram
tools.description: Plot an eye diagram by overlaying successive segments of a signal, revealing intersymbol interference, timing jitter and noise margin. A wide open eye means good signal quality and a clear sampling instant. The period argument is usually two or three times the samples per symbol.
tools.usage:
eyediagram(x, n)
eyediagram(x, n, period)
eyediagram(x, n, period, offset)
h = eyediagram(x, n, period, offset, plotstring)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Signal to display; complex signals get separate in-phase and quadrature panels.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of samples per trace, typically 2 or 3 times the samples per symbol.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Time span of the horizontal axis.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Sample offset of the trace start.

tools.name: comm.ConstellationDiagram
tools.description: A scope System object that displays a live, updating constellation diagram as a simulation runs. It can overlay the reference constellation and compute EVM and MER measurements directly in the scope. Much more informative than scatterplot for streaming simulations.
tools.usage:
cd = comm.ConstellationDiagram(Name, Value)
cd(x)
release(cd)

parameters.name: 'ReferenceConstellation'
parameters.description: Ideal constellation points to overlay, e.g. qammod(0:15, 16, 'UnitAveragePower', true).

parameters.name: 'SamplesPerSymbol'
parameters.description: Oversampling factor of the input.

parameters.name: 'ShowReferenceConstellation'
parameters.description: Logical; draw the ideal points.

parameters.name: 'Title' / 'XLimits' / 'YLimits'
parameters.description: Display appearance.

parameters.name: 'MeasurementInterval'
parameters.description: Number of symbols over which EVM/MER are computed.
